title: He descended (CCC 632–637)
hookLine: he went to the dead to open heaven for the just who went before

cards: Friday evening, the body is laid in a tomb and a stone is rolled across the door. The women go home and, as Luke puts it, rest on the sabbath according to the commandment. Then Sunday morning, the empty tomb.
In between, the Gospels say almost nothing. Catholic churches keep Holy Saturday bare and quiet. And yet the Apostles' Creed has a line for exactly that silence.
Between buried and rose again, it says: he descended into hell. It's a strange line to say out loud.

teach.h: HELL HERE MEANS THE PLACE OF THE DEAD.
teach.b: Day sixty-seven kept Holy Saturday's quiet; today, the Creed's line for it. First, what hell means there.

Scripture, the Catechism says, calls the place of the dead hell: Sheol in Hebrew, Hades in Greek, the realm of those who died before Christ, deprived of the sight of God, the just and the wicked alike, all waiting.

So the line isn't saying Jesus went to the place of the damned. The Catechism is precise: he did not go down to free the damned, or to destroy the hell of damnation, but to free the just who had gone before him.
Second, it says he truly died: raised from the dead means he had truly been among the dead, as people die. Third, what he did there.

teach.h: PREACHED TO THE SPIRITS IN PRISON.
teach.b: The first letter of Peter says that Christ, in the Douay-Rheims, "preached to those spirits that were in prison," and a little later that the gospel was preached even to the dead.
The Catechism calls this the last phase of his mission: the good news reaching people of every time and place, all the way back.

Then it quotes what it calls an ancient homily for Holy Saturday, where Christ goes down looking for Adam, the first man, like a shepherd looking for a lost sheep, takes him by the hand, and tells him to rise.

Some icons of the resurrection paint that moment: Christ standing on broken gates, pulling Adam and Eve up out of their tombs. Holy Saturday looks silent from above. In Catholic teaching, down below it was loud.

how: Catholics profess Christ's descent to the dead in the Apostles' Creed, keep Holy Saturday as a quiet day of waiting at the tomb, and pray for the dead, above all at Mass and in November.

games.q: you're painting an icon of the resurrection. you could paint the empty tomb, or the risen Christ alone. there's a third choice. what is it?
o: the guards asleep at the tomb
Christ pulling Adam and Eve up out of their tombs
games.why: some icons of the resurrection show Christ among the dead, raising Adam and Eve by the hand, as in the old Holy Saturday homily.

practice: Bring to mind those who came before you, a grandparent, a great-grandmother whose name you only half know, and say the names you have, quietly, letting a place, a language or a recipe stand in for the ones nobody kept.
If you pray, pray for them, as Catholics pray for the dead; if you don't, simply hold one thing of theirs you still carry.

wordCard.voice: He descended. The Creed's line for Holy Saturday: Christ among the dead, freeing the just. Today's word.
